claims.text: An ultra-thin Ni-based interlayer will improve adhesion of an HEA coating to a Cu substrate.
The Ni-based interlayer establishes a graded, chemically compatible interface between Cu and the HEA.
The initial substrate is clean Cu with minimal surface oxides and defects.
The proposed interlayer is Ni-based and approximately tens of nanometers thick.
The HEA coating is deposited after the Ni-based interlayer.
Moderate-temperature post-deposition heat treatment will promote interdiffusion and metallurgical bonding.
The Ni interlayer accommodates lattice mismatch between Cu and the HEA.
The Ni interlayer facilitates coherent grain boundaries at the coating–substrate interface.
The Ni interlayer produces a graded chemical composition between Cu and the HEA.
Nickel chemically bonds with Cu and thereby reduces interfacial energy.
The Ni interlayer improves wetting of the subsequently deposited HEA.
The intermediate chemical and crystallographic properties of Ni help prevent brittle intermetallic phases that would degrade adhesion.
HEAs possess superior wear resistance relative to conventional alloys.
Adding the Ni interlayer will improve the wear resistance of the HEA-on-Cu system relative to direct HEA deposition on Cu.
Adding the Ni interlayer will reduce delamination under mechanical and thermal stress.
Direct deposition of HEA onto Cu without an interlayer typically produces poor bonding.
Directly deposited HEA on Cu undergoes accelerated wear because of mismatched interfacial chemistry and structure.
The adhesion benefit requires the interlayer to remain ultra-thin and predominantly Ni.
An excessively thick or compositionally deviating interlayer could form unwanted phases and negate adhesion benefits.
Failure to obtain statistically significant gains in shear strength and wear resistance, or observation of deleterious interfacial phases, would falsify the hypothesis.
